title: Running the Claude Agent SDK on Cloudflare Sandbox Containers
summary: Michael Golden walks through a working app that runs the Claude Agent SDK inside Cloudflare Sandbox containers.

chapters.title: Workers, D1, R2 and Durable Objects

learn: Golden says the Claude Agent SDK gives an app the power of Claude Code without building and orchestrating an agent on LangGraph and LangChain.
The deployed stack uses Cloudflare Workers for the front end and back end, Sandbox containers to run the SDK in TypeScript, a D1 SQLite database, R2 object storage, and Clerk for authentication.
In the demo, a React app lets users pick Sonnet, Haiku or Opus, create skills and sub-agents scoped to projects, and see hooks stream back from the agent.
A live prompt asks the agent to research orbital data, write Python and output a GIF simulating the solar system, running entirely inside the sandbox.
Golden explains that agents need to execute code, need a file system, and need one isolated instance per user, and that runs can last 40 to 50 minutes.
Sandbox SDK is built on containers and Durable Objects, and the image is Ubuntu with Node, Bun, and Python libraries such as Matplotlib, NumPy and Pandas.
